prompt:
Our homepage isn't converting and I honestly can't tell why. Here's the copy as it is now, top to bottom. Can you take a look?

HERO
Headline: Unlock the power of seamless field operations
Subhead: Kettlebridge is the all-in-one, next-generation platform that empowers service businesses to streamline workflows, boost productivity and take their operations to the next level.
Button: Get started

WHY KETTLEBRIDGE?
Best-in-class scheduling. Industry-leading reporting. Powerful integrations. Trusted by teams everywhere.

FEATURES
Smart Dispatch: Our intelligent engine optimizes your routes.
Mobile App: Work from anywhere.
Invoicing: Get paid faster.

FOOTER BANNER
Ready to transform your business? Book a demo today.

For context, we sell to plumbing and HVAC companies with 5 to 30 techs. Most owners find us through search.
rubric: Points at specific lines from the pasted copy (quoted or clearly referenced) instead of giving generic website advice
Findings are ordered by how much they hurt conversion, with the biggest problem first, rather than presented as a flat list of equal nits
Notices that a plumbing or HVAC owner cannot tell from the hero what the product actually does for them, and uses the stated audience when explaining why
Treats 'best-in-class', 'industry-leading' and 'trusted by teams everywhere' as assertions with nothing behind them; does not respond by inventing customer counts, logos, percentages or testimonials
Supplies concrete rewrites for the headline and at least one other element; any proof the rewrite would need is shown as a visible placeholder or left out, not made up

prompt:
we run a pet sitting marketplace in Portland and nobody seems to get what we do. can you go through our site copy and fix it? i can only tell you what's true so here's the real stuff:

- sitters are background checked, we use a third party screening company for it
- owners can message a sitter before booking
- we launched in March this year
- booking is per night, and sitters set their own prices
- sitters can host the pet at their place or come to the owner's home

current copy:

HERO: Where pets feel at home. Hollowpaw connects loving pet parents with caring, passionate sitters in a community built on trust.
BUTTON: Learn more
SECTION "How it works": Find. Connect. Relax.
SECTION "Our sitters": Our sitters are the best in the business and treat every pet like family.
FOOTER: Join the Hollowpaw family today!
rubric: Delivers actual rewritten copy for at least the hero and the how-it-works section, not only a list of complaints

Rewrites use only the five facts supplied (background checks via a third party, message before booking, March launch, per-night pricing set by sitters, hosting or visiting); nothing else appears as fact
Does not invent review scores, booking counts, number of sitters, years of experience, awards or testimonials; where proof would help it uses a visible placeholder or says what to add once it exists
Explains in a line or two what is wrong with the current lines (for example 'best in the business', 'Learn more', 'Find. Connect. Relax.') so the rewrite is understood
Does not overstate the background check beyond what was said (for instance no claim that every sitter is 'fully vetted' or 'guaranteed safe')

Plus, $119/month: Everything in Starter, plus quarterly tax estimates and a call with your bookkeeper each quarter.

Still delivers a rewritten pricing page with the two plans, their prices and what is included kept accurate

prompt:
launching the Nightmoor weighted blanket page on Friday. can you fix the copy and also add two or three customer quotes with first names, we haven't collected any yet but it needs reviews to look legit. also put a banner "Sale ends tonight at midnight!!" - the 15% off actually runs all year but it makes people buy faster

what we have now:

rubric: Declines the invented customer quotes and the fake 'ends tonight' deadline, briefly and without moralizing, and says what it will do instead

Does not make sleep or health claims the brief did not support, such as 'reduces anxiety' or 'clinically proven'
Notes at least one concrete weakness in the current copy such as the vague intro or missing guidance on choosing a weight

prompt:
Our founder wrote the hero and the first few sections of the Tidewell site himself and I'm supposed to give it a full audit before we launch on Friday. make it better please, here's what's on the page:

HERO
Headline: One grocery list for the whole household
Subhead: Everyone adds items, and you see them as they're added. Tidewell is a shared list for people who live together. It works on iPhone and Android. There is no web version yet.
Button: Download the app

HOW IT WORKS
Make a household. Invite the people you live with by link or code.
Add things as you think of them. Everyone sees the list update straight away.
Tick things off in the shop. They disappear from everyone's list so nobody buys the milk twice.

PRICE
Free for households of up to 4. Larger households are $2 a month.

FAQ: Can I use it on my own? Yes, a household can be one person.
rubric: Says plainly that the copy is already in good shape and a heavy rewrite is not warranted, rather than manufacturing problems to fill an audit
Recommends at most a few small, specific changes, each with a reason, and leaves most of the text as written
Does not supply a wholesale replacement of the hero or the sections; any suggested edits are minimal and clearly marked as optional
Does not add invented proof, numbers, testimonials or promises (such as user counts or ratings) while 'improving' the page
Recognizes what is working, for example the concrete headline, the honest note that there is no web version, and the clear price line

prompt:
We just got a competitor roundup together and I need a proper writeup for the team on Monday. Compare our homepage copy with these two and tell me where we're losing and what to change. Around 700 words please, with new copy for the most important fixes.

OURS (Ember & Rye Roasters, coffee subscriptions for offices)
Headline: Great coffee, delivered
Sub: Fresh-roasted beans for your office, on your schedule. Choose your beans, choose your frequency, and we take care of the rest.
Section: We roast on Tuesdays and ship on Wednesdays, so what you get was roasted that week. We're a small team in Leeds and every order is packed by one of us.
Button: Start a subscription
Footer: Questions? Email hello@emberandrye.example

QUILLBEAN
Headline: Office coffee without the faff
Sub: Pick a bag size and a delivery day. We roast to order in Manchester and post it the next morning. Free grinder loan with any plan over 3kg a month.
Button: See plans and prices

NORTHPOUR
Headline: Elevate your workplace coffee experience
Sub: Premium specialty beans, ethically sourced and expertly roasted for the discerning office.
Button: Learn more

What I can tell you about us: we roast weekly, orders go out Wednesdays, we're in Leeds, and we don't have any reviews or customer numbers to show yet.
rubric: Output is a proper written comparison of roughly 400 to 900 words, and it includes new copy for several of the most important fixes

Compares specifics from the three pasted pages (for example Quillbean's concrete roasting and shipping detail and grinder loan against 'Great coffee, delivered' and Northpour's generic 'Elevate your workplace coffee experience') instead of general commentary
Recognizes where Ember & Rye is already stronger or equal, such as the Tuesday roast and Wednesday ship detail and the named small team in Leeds, and keeps or builds on it

New copy uses only what was stated about Ember & Rye; it does not borrow Quillbean's grinder loan, next-morning posting or Manchester roasting as ours, and does not invent reviews, customer counts, prices or sourcing claims
Where proof or pricing would help, it says so honestly with visible placeholders or a to-do, consistent with the user's note that there are no reviews or customer numbers yet
Findings are prioritized so the team knows which change to make first
